text.title: Market Analysis Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a real seller set competes for the budget line, whether the question is sizing rather than structure, and whether a pass/fail boundary test can be written and adjudicated — to a full boundary-segments-forces analysis, a halt on the boundary, or a skip to sizing or switch-interview work.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there a set of sellers competing for the same budget line, or a single named account / captive internal customer?

branch.when: the "market" is one named account, a captive internal customer, or a mandated supplier with no alternatives

conclusion.verdict: skip; there is no seller set to analyse. Run account planning or a stakeholder map instead

branch.when: multiple independent sellers compete for the same buyers and the same budget
branch.question: Is the decision waiting on a number — how big is it — or on structure: who is in, how it splits, what is moving?

branch.when: the only open question is market size, and boundary and segmentation are already settled

conclusion.verdict: skip; route to market-research-tam-sam-som — sizing does not need the full structural analysis

branch.when: boundary, segmentation, growth or regulatory forces are genuinely contested
branch.question: Can the market boundary be written as a pass/fail test over buyer type, need served, substitutability, geography and channel — and applied to 3 named borderline companies with an in/out verdict each?

branch.when: only a category noun is available and no incumbent budget line or substitute can be named for the product

conclusion.verdict: halt; draft the inclusion test and adjudicate 3 borderline companies before segmenting. If no substitute or incumbent budget line exists at all, route to jtbd-switch-interview first

branch.when: an inclusion test is writable and 3 borderline companies can be adjudicated on record

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; partition segments demand-side so sizes reconcile within 10%, date every growth figure, and give each force the decision it flips
